title: Emit + ingest `route` dimension in telemetry/metering pipeline (cardinality-safe)
creator: Logan Wright
project: In-console usage insights (cost drivers by route)
description:
Epic

We need to plumb a canonical `route` dimension from request entry points (SDK + gateway) through metering and into the analytics pipeline so downstream aggregates/APIs can power the new “usage insights” console views.

This epic covers:
- defining the event schema changes + compatibility strategy
- implementing ingestion + normalization/guardrails to prevent cardinality blowups
- ensuring correct attribution when smart routing/model fallback occurs mid-request
- adding pipeline-level monitoring for route dimension health (coverage, invalids, rollups)

Out of scope for this ticket
- building the aggregates/API endpoints (ENG-8422/8423/8424)
- export jobs + auditing (ENG-8425)

Background / references
- Confluence ADR: route dimension definition + normalization (adr-route-dimension-definition-and-normalization)
- Confluence standards: cost attribution cardinality guardrails

Problem
Today metering events can attribute cost/latency by org/project/model/deployment, but not by developer-defined “route”. Customers can’t answer “what endpoints are costing us the most?” without external instrumentation.

Proposed approach
1) Route sources (in priority order)
- SDK-provided route: clients can provide a stable identifier (e.g., "chat.completions", "support-bot.answer")
- Gateway-derived route: for HTTP gateway traffic, derive from the route template (NOT raw path) when available (e.g., "/v1/chat/completions" or "/apps/:appId/agents/:agentId")
- Fallback: "unknown" (explicitly tracked)

2) Schema additions (metering + perf events)
Add fields (names pending final contract; keep backward compatible):
- route: normalized canonical route string (bounded length; allowed charset)
- route_source: sdk | gateway | unknown
- route_is_rolled_up: boolean (true if we had to bucket/roll up)
- route_hash: stable hash of the *pre-rollup* normalized route, used for internal debugging/uniqueness checks without storing the raw value long-term

3) Normalization (performed at ingestion boundary)
- trim whitespace; lowercase
- max length 96 chars (truncate deterministically)
- allowed chars: [a-z0-9._/:-] (replace others with "_")
- collapse multiple consecutive slashes
- disallow dynamic segments guidance is docs-side; ingestion additionally detects obvious high-cardinality patterns (uuid-ish, long numeric ids) and rolls up

4) Cardinality guardrails
Hard limits are required because route is developer-controlled and can explode dimension cardinality.
- per-org/day unique route budget (starting proposal): 2,500 unique routes/day
- per-org/hour unique route budget: 500 unique routes/hour
- when budget exceeded:
  - continue counting cost/latency but route is set to "__other__" (route_is_rolled_up=true)
  - emit a structured internal metric + log event with org/project + counts (no raw route string)
- high-cardinality heuristic rollups before the budget is hit:
  - if route contains >2 numeric segments longer than 6 digits => roll up
  - if route contains uuid-like pattern => roll up

5) Attribution correctness across model fallback
We must keep `route` stable across the full request lifecycle, even if routing changes the model mid-request.
- route is attached to request context at entry, then copied into all per-segment metering events
- for multi-model requests: each model-segment metering event gets the same route; downstream aggregates can show breakdown by route+model

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Metering event schema supports route + route_source + route_is_rolled_up (behind schema versioning)
- [ ] Route arrives in raw telemetry topic and in long-term metering store for >= 99% of requests that include route tagging / are gateway-derived
- [ ] Cardinality guardrails prevent ingestion blowups; we can demonstrate stable memory/CPU in pipeline under synthetic "bad route" load test
- [ ] Unknown route rate is visible as a metric (by deployment mode), with a basic alert threshold proposal
- [ ] Backward compatibility: older clients/gateways that don’t send route continue to meter correctly
- [ ] Security review complete for: whether route can contain sensitive data; how we handle hashing; retention of raw route (should not store raw beyond normalized + bounded)

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: customers include PII/user IDs in route
  - Mitigation: strict normalization + heuristics + rollup; docs + SDK warnings; budget-based bucketing; do not persist raw route beyond normalized/bounded
- Risk: route template derivation differs across gateways / frameworks
  - Mitigation: route_source field + coverage metrics; add test matrix for gateway route templates; treat mismatched templates as gateway bug
- Risk: performance overhead on hot path
  - Mitigation: normalize once at ingress; avoid regex-heavy logic; use fast path checks; keep hashing optional / sampling

Implementation plan (high-level)
Phase A: Ingress plumbing
- SDKs: standard header/param is implemented in SDK workstream (ENG-8432); this epic ensures server reads it
- Gateway: derive route template and attach to context (Amara + Thomas)

Phase B: Telemetry + metering
- Update request context struct to include route fields
- Update metering event emitters to include route fields
- Update ingestion/ETL to parse, validate, normalize, and apply rollup/budget logic

Phase C: Observability
- Dashboards: unknown route %, rolled-up route %, per-org unique route counts
- Alarms: sustained spikes in rolled-up/unknown; ingestion lag correlated with route explosion attempts

Links
- PR (in progress): redwood#15432 (route dimension plumbed through request context + metering events)
- Related epics: ENG-8422 (aggregate tables), ENG-8423/8424 (APIs), ENG-8425 (exports)
comments: 2026-01-21 (Logan Wright): Kickoff with Nadia/Caleb/Thomas + Console team. Agreement that route must be attached at ingress and treated as a first-class dimension in metering (not derived in analytics later). Biggest open item: exact guardrail thresholds (need to tune with SRE).

2026-01-28 (Thomas Baird): Proposed guardrail mechanics: per-org/hour unique route budget + rollup to __other__. We should NOT drop events; we should still meter, just bucket the dimension. Also recommend emitting a counter for “route_budget_exceeded” keyed by org/project/deployment_mode to make abuse/misconfig visible.

2026-02-03 (Nadia Rahman): Implemented schema changes locally; route normalization currently uses a lightweight sanitizer + truncation. Added uuid detection using a simple segment check (hex+dash length). Need review from Amara on gateway template extraction so we don’t double-normalize.

2026-02-07 (Allison Grant): SRE ask: ensure we have a single metric for unique route cardinality *before* aggregation (raw ingestion), otherwise we won’t catch pipeline pain until too late. Also add alerting for sudden increase in rolled-up routes for a given org (potential customer regression).

2026-02-12 (Marcus Lin): Security review notes (preliminary): route should be treated as customer-provided metadata and could contain sensitive info. Strong preference to not store any pre-normalized raw value. If we need uniqueness debugging, store only hash of normalized value and sample logs only in internal env.

2026-02-18 (Nadia Rahman): PR redwood#15432 is up. Remaining TODOs: (1) finalize length limit (96 vs 128), (2) make route_hash optional behind config flag, (3) add ingestion-side budget enforcement (currently only metrics).
